notes: Design inferred: a case review of surveillance cases comparing two periods. Average annual percent increases are arithmetic means of yearly percent changes (e.g., 54.4, 21.3, −9.5 → 22.1). The 2020-only comparison (p = 0.006) is presumably also the chi-square test; pandemic disruptions offered as explanations have no equity framing.
view_issues: Text speaks of the 'rate' of syphilis and the caption of 'prevalence', but the table gives only case counts. 2018 percentages (3 = 23.1%, 5 = 38.5%) imply a denominator of 13, not 11 total CS cases; 2016 1 of 12 shown as 8.2%.
